public_rationale: The evidence documents real learning risks, widespread errors in AI news responses, and large-scale sexual-image abuse. It does not establish the full conjunction at the asserted scale. Educational experiments show that design changes outcomes, including benefits. The large image estimate measures sexualized content without determining consent. Official findings strengthen the abuse component, but cannot settle the educational and information-system claims.
limitations: The forceful language has no supplied quantitative threshold.
Localized educational benefits do not refute broader harms; localized harms do not establish systemic destruction.
The Canadian findings were published after the post but concern the earlier incident.

statement.excerpt: It is ripping apart our educational system and our information ecosphere, and flooding the zone with nonconsensual deepfake porn.
statement.document_title: Turns out Generative AI was a scam

our_interpretation: Ripping apart means widespread, substantial damage to the functioning of education and the information environment, rather than the existence of individual harms.
Flooding the zone means large-scale production or dissemination of nonconsensual sexual deepfakes.
The conjunction commits to all three components. I assess the state described as of February 23, 2026; later publications may document earlier events.
No country is specified. Evidence from individual institutions or jurisdictions cannot alone establish system-wide damage.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes substantial, widespread educational and information-system damage caused by generative AI, together with large-scale nonconsensual sexual deepfake production or dissemination.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence demonstrates that a material component of the asserted widespread damage is absent or materially overstated. Benefits in isolated settings alone would not establish this.

evidence.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, indexed by PubMed
evidence.explanation: The Turkish school experiment found lower subsequent unassisted performance with unrestricted assistance, while safeguards largely removed the harm. This earlier, localized experiment establishes a possible mechanism, not the claimed system-wide state in February 2026.

The multinational evaluation supports a substantial information-integrity problem in AI news responses. It does not measure overall deterioration of the information environment or establish that the system is being ripped apart.

evidence.locator: Grok generated an estimated 3 million photorealistic sexualized images
evidence.explanation: A sampled estimate puts sexualized-image generation at approximately three million over the period ending January 8. The study explicitly did not determine consent, and its definition includes swimwear, so this is not a count of nonconsensual pornography.

evidence.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
evidence.explanation: The official investigation found failures to obtain valid consent and inadequate safeguards concerning the widespread late-December and early-January incident. It supports the nonconsensual-abuse component, without making every image in the separate volume estimate nonconsensual pornography.

A randomized Harvard physics experiment found benefits from a deliberately designed tutor. It is material caution against treating educational harm as uniform, but this earlier, localized result does not disprove widespread damage elsewhere.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative longitudinal or causal evidence of substantial educational and information-system deterioration, plus consent-sensitive measurements of sexual deepfake dissemination.
